answers.solution: To calculate the simple interest, I'll use the formula I = P × i × n. Given: P = $1,000, i = 5% = 0.05, n = 3 years. Calculation: I = 1000 × 0.05 × 3 = $150. Therefore, I will earn $150 in interest after 3 years.

Given values: Principal = $1,000, Interest rate = 5%, Time = 3 years. First, I convert 5% to decimal: 0.05. Using the simple interest formula I = P × i × n: I = 1000 × 0.05 × 3. Step by step: 1000 × 0.05 = 50, then 50 × 3 = 150. The total interest earned is $150.

Simple interest calculation: P = $1,000, i = 5% (or 0.05 in decimal), n = 3 years. Using I = P × i × n: Interest = $1,000 × 0.05 × 3 = $150. After 3 years, the interest earned on the savings account will be $150.
